summary: Fresh FOC Heat research for the Sep. 7, 2026 FOC window. No current BUY is justified after re-research. The strongest candidates are 12-Foot Skeleton #1, You'll Never Leave This Place Alive #1, Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, and Star Trek: Zero Point #1, but each lacks sufficient issue-specific aftermarket demand/supply evidence to clear the project's BUY threshold. Several recognizable-IP or variant-heavy books are PASS because hype, ratios, or franchise strength do not establish an investment edge.
orderingWindow: FOC is Monday, Sep. 7, 2026. PRH and Comic Previews independently list Sep. 7 as the FOC date. M&M Comics states weekly FOC preorders are due 7pm Central every Monday; that is 8pm Eastern for an Indiana/Eastern-time buyer, but individual retailers may impose earlier deadlines. One retailer currently shows Sep. 6, so do not assume a universal retail cutoff time.

books.title: 12-FOOT SKELETON #1
books.creators: Tim Seeley and Aaron Campbell (writers), Ben Templesmith (interior art/colors); Templesmith cover A; Seeley 1:10 and signed 1:20 incentive covers
verifiedFacts: Ignition Press identifies 12-Foot Skeleton as a five-issue limited series.
PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Sep. 7, 2026 FOC, 32 pages and $4.99 cover price.
The premise is a Halloween horror story involving a 12-foot lawn skeleton, two 12-year-old protagonists and an unusual personal connection to the monster.
PRH lists Cover C as a 1:10 Tim Seeley incentive; retailer data also lists a signed 1:20 Seeley edition.
marketEvidence: Ben Templesmith's original 30 Days of Night #1 has substantial completed-sale evidence, including multiple 2026 sales from roughly $65 to $250, showing that his work can anchor durable collector demand when attached to a genuine key.
That evidence is creator/key evidence, not proof that 12-Foot Skeleton #1 will appreciate.
Current retailers are still openly offering standard copies below cover, including $3.99-$4.24 listings, which is not evidence of scarcity.
Key Collector's current guide for the unreleased 1:20 lists low/mid/high values of $1/$2/$6; these are guide estimates, not completed sales and therefore are not treated as demand proof.
books.thesis: This is the most interesting pure horror/speculative book in the window because the Halloween timing, recognizable horror creator and limited-series format give it a plausible collector niche. The problem is supply evidence: standard copies are widely available below cover and there is no issue-specific completed-sale history. WATCH rather than BUY. If later acquired for $3.99 or less, one standard copy would have a defensible asymmetric downside, but multiple copies or ratio speculation is not justified.
unknowns: Whether the series develops a durable collector following
Whether the story contains a future key/first appearance

books.title: YOU'LL NEVER LEAVE THIS PLACE ALIVE #1
books.creators: Collin Kelly and Jackson Lanzing (writers), Heather Vaughan (artist), Clayton Cowles (letterer)
verifiedFacts: PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Sep. 7 FOC, 48 pages and $4.99 cover price.
The story is a horror mystery about five young people raised in an isolated community whose apparent sanctuary hides a lethal secret.
PRH lists a broad cover program including a 1:10 Joshua Hixson incentive and a 1:25 Hixson full-art incentive.
marketEvidence: Multiple advance reviews published in late August and early September are strongly positive, including ratings of 9/10 and 10/10; this is a real demand signal but not aftermarket evidence.
Current retailer listings show standard copies at or below cover, so there is no verified pre-release scarcity premium.
No completed-sale evidence exists for the unreleased issue.
The 1:10 and 1:25 structure could create scarcity, but the project does not assume that scarcity will translate into demand.
books.thesis: The strongest new-IP WATCH on the week. The early critical response is unusually consistent and the horror premise has collector-friendly characteristics, but there is still no completed-sale evidence and retailer availability does not indicate scarcity. Do not buy ratios at FOC. If a standard copy can be acquired at $3.99 or less, one copy is reasonable as a low-cost speculation; otherwise wait for post-release sales.
unknowns: Whether any character/event becomes a durable key

books.title: STARSHIP GODZILLA: INVASION X [KAI-SEI ERA] #1
verifiedFacts: IDW/PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Sep. 7 FOC, 36 pages and $4.99 cover price.
It is a five-issue follow-up to the 2025 Starship Godzilla series and is designed to remain accessible to new readers.
IDW's official announcement says pre-orders are due Sep. 7, 2026.
The issue has four listed covers, including Joëlle Jones, Gavin Fullerton and Louie Joyce variants.
marketEvidence: The original Starship Godzilla #1 has completed-sale history, but standard copies are generally near cover: PriceCharting shows recent completed sales around $4.19-$9.49 and a current ungraded estimate around $5.73.
A Chris Gooch variant has a documented completed sale at $0.99, reinforcing that creator/variant status alone does not create durable demand.
A specific NRG exclusive of the original issue has stronger sales, but it is a separately limited exclusive and cannot be used as proof for the standard sequel issue.
An advance review published Sep. 2 is positive, providing current reader-interest evidence but not aftermarket evidence.
books.thesis: Godzilla is a powerful IP and the first Starship Godzilla series gives this sequel a real demand baseline. Unfortunately, the baseline is weak for standard copies and does not show sustained premiums. The sequel's standard $4.99 entry is acceptable, but there is no demonstrated scarcity/demand imbalance. WATCH one standard copy only if acquired at cover or below; no variant chasing.
unknowns: Whether the Kai-Sei Era builds a durable collector market
Whether the sequel contains a new key appearance

books.title: STAR TREK: ZERO POINT #1
books.creators: Charlie Jane Anders (writer), Isaac Sánchez González (artist), Valeria Favoccia (Cover A)
verifiedFacts: PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Sep. 7 FOC, 32 pages and $4.99 cover price.
IDW describes it as a tie-in series to the new Star Trek (2026) line, following Raffi Musiker and a classified mission involving a powerful artificial intelligence.
The issue has a broad eight-cover program, including photo, foil, IDW Goes Dark and other variants.
marketEvidence: Two independent advance reviews published Sep. 2 are strongly positive, including a review calling it a great beginning with substantial potential and emphasizing its mix of familiar and new material.

Past Star Trek #1 issues show that franchise recognition alone does not guarantee appreciation: the 1989 DC #1 has many 2026 completed sales around roughly $2-$15, while older key first issues perform differently because of historical significance.
There is no completed-sale evidence for Zero Point #1 because it is unreleased.
The broad variant program increases collector attention but also makes supply risk substantial.
books.thesis: This is a legitimate collector-interest book, particularly for Star Trek fans and buyers responding to the 60th-anniversary publishing push. It is not yet a demonstrated investment. The clean $4.99 entry is the main reason to keep it on WATCH; no premium variant is justified before issue-specific market evidence exists.
unknowns: Whether Zero Point becomes a durable key
Which variants, if any, retain premiums

books.title: MAGIC: THE GATHERING: UNTOLD STORIES--LILIANA #1
books.creators: Torunn Grønbekk (writer), Nataliia Rerekina (artist/cover A), Abigail Larson (variant)
verifiedFacts: PRH lists Oct. 14, 2026 on-sale, Sep. 7 FOC, 32 pages and $4.99 cover price.
This is a four-issue series centered on Liliana Vess and her pact with four demons, set partly on Innistrad.
The issue has three listed covers at standard cover price.
marketEvidence: The directly comparable Magic: The Gathering: Untold Stories--Elspeth #1 has numerous completed 2026 sales clustered around $3-$8, with many at $4.49-$4.99.
That completed-sale history shows an active collector market but no reliable standard-copy premium for this Dark Horse line.
No completed-sale evidence exists for the unreleased Liliana issue.
books.thesis: The character is important within Magic, but the closest direct comic-market precedent is not strong enough. PASS for investment at FOC; buy only as a reading/collection purchase or later if an actual demand imbalance emerges.

books.title: SUNDER #1
books.creators: Pierre-Alexandre Comtois (writer/artist), Mark Englert (colorist), Buddy Beaudoin (letterer); Christian Ward and Daniele Serra variants
verifiedFacts: Mad Cave lists Sunder #1 as a pre-order with $6.99-$8.99 variant pricing.
The comic follows Zeek, an orphan in a remote monastery who discovers a magical book, combining magic, science fiction, adventure and monsters.
The current single-issue release is a 48-page comic; FOC is Sep. 7 and release is Sep. 30.
marketEvidence: Mad Cave cites positive critical response, including a Kirkus quote and other review praise, but this is not completed-sale evidence.
The underlying Sunder graphic novel has been available since 2025, yet no reliable completed-sale evidence establishing a premium for the property was found in this research pass.
Current pre-orders are openly available at standard/discounted pricing, providing no scarcity signal.
books.thesis: The property has a real publishing history and positive critical response, but the single-issue investment case is unsupported. The $6.99 entry is too high for an unproven standard copy and the $8.99 foil is even harder to justify. PASS.
unknowns: Whether existing graphic-novel readers convert to comic collectors

books.title: SUPERMAN KINGDOM OF ZOD SPECIAL #1
books.creators: Joshua Williamson, Mark Waid, Dan Slott and Sophie Campbell (writers); Paolo Villanelli, Bruno Frenda, David Messina and Sophie Campbell (artists); Dan Mora cover
verifiedFacts: Current retailer/catalog data lists Sep. 30 release and Sep. 7 FOC at $5.99.
It is the conclusion to Kingdom of Zod, featuring Superman, Supergirl, Zod and Ursa.
marketEvidence: No completed-sale evidence exists because the issue is unreleased.
As a concluding special rather than a fresh first issue, the structural investment case is weaker than the strongest #1 candidates.
The large established Superman audience is offset by the lack of demonstrated scarcity or a specific key.
books.thesis: Potentially important to readers of Kingdom of Zod, but there is no verified investment edge. PASS.
unknowns: Whether the conclusion contains a durable key event

books.title: BEWARE THE WITCH'S SHADOW: MONSTER BASH #1
books.creators: Various writers/artists; Puis Calzada and Dan Parsons variant art
verifiedFacts: Current retailer/catalog data lists Sep. 30 release and Sep. 7 FOC, with standard cover at $4.99 and $9.99 variants.
The anthology presents three black-and-white mature horror stories in a retro horror-magazine style.
marketEvidence: Key Collector's current guide for the unreleased issue shows low/mid/high values around $1/$2/$5 for the main issue and similarly modest guide ranges for variants; these are guide estimates, not completed sales.
No completed-sale evidence was found for the unreleased issue.
The $9.99 variants create a high acquisition hurdle without corresponding demand evidence.
books.thesis: Horror is a viable collector niche, but this issue currently has neither demonstrated scarcity nor demand. PASS.

ledgerNotes: All prior predictions remain unchanged; no historical prediction was rewritten based on user purchase behavior.
Minotaur #1 remains LOSS; Black Star #1 remains LOSS; all existing PENDING predictions remain PENDING.
The Aug. 31 books from the prior report are now treated as POST-FOC opportunities or historical watch items and are not current BUY candidates.
Four new Sep. 4 WATCH evaluations were added: 12-Foot Skeleton #1, You'll Never Leave This Place Alive #1, Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, and Star Trek: Zero Point #1.
No user purchase or position is inferred from any recommendation.
methodologyChanges: No BUY is issued when the best available evidence consists of reviews, franchise strength or creator history without issue-specific aftermarket evidence.
Retailer pre-order availability below cover is treated as a supply/entry-price warning, not as scarcity evidence.
Completed sales for prior issues are used only as supporting evidence and never as proof that a new issue will appreciate.
Ratio incentives are not recommended unless demand evidence supports the premium; scarcity alone is insufficient.
